q: 1. The liquidity index of soil is given by
explain: Liquidity index (Il) is calculated as the natural water content minus the plastic limit, divided by the plasticity index.

q: 2. Coarse grained soil contains material half of which is larger than
explain: As per soil classification (IS/USCS), a soil is termed coarse-grained if more than 50% of material by weight is retained on the 75-micron (0.075 mm) sieve.

q: 3. Liquid and plastic limit exists in the soil type
explain: Atterberg limits (liquid limit, plastic limit) are meaningful only for fine-grained, plastic soils such as clay, which exhibit plastic behaviour with changing moisture.

q: 4. Bearing capacity of soil depends up on the particle
explain: Bearing capacity is influenced by particle shape (interlocking), cohesion, and size (gradation/density) — collectively all these factors matter.

q: 5. In the modified proctor test the drop height of the rammer is .............
explain: The Modified Proctor test uses a heavier rammer dropped from 45 cm, giving higher compactive effort than the Standard Proctor test.

q: 6. Effective size of the particle is
explain: Effective size is defined as D10 — the particle size corresponding to 10% passing on the grain size distribution curve.

q: 7. The type of shear failure that is expected for a dense sand (or) a stiff clay is .............
explain: Dense sands and stiff clays, being incompressible and strong, exhibit general shear failure with a well-defined failure surface and peak resistance.

q: 8. The type of shear failure that can be expected for a loose sand (or) a soft clay is .............
explain: Loose sands and soft clays are highly compressible and tend to fail by punching shear, with large settlements and no distinct failure surface.

q: 9. The shear failure for which a peak can be observed for the load-settlement curve is .............
explain: Per the reference key, this is attributed to punching shear failure characteristics in the load-settlement response.

q: 10. Stoke's law is applicable to particles upto ............. effective diameter.
explain: Stoke's Law is valid for fine particles up to about 0.2 mm, but sedimentation analysis specifically applies it for particles as fine as around 0.002 mm.

q: 11. The uniformity coefficient of soil is
explain: Uniformity coefficient Cu = D60/D10, a measure of the range of particle sizes present (gradation).

q: 12. Which of the following is a cohesion less soil?
explain: Sand particles lack the electrochemical bonding of clay minerals, making sand a cohesionless soil.

q: 13. Cohesive soils are generally
explain: Fine-grained cohesive soils (clays) typically exhibit both plasticity (deformability without cracking) and compressibility (volume reduction under load).

q: 14. Finest grain particles are contained in .............
explain: Clay has the smallest particle size among these soil types, generally below 0.002 mm.

q: 15. Clays containing organic matter are made suitable for stabilization, by first adding a percentage of .............
explain: Per the reference key, resins are used as the initial additive to counteract organic matter before further stabilization of such clays.

q: 16. The standard penetration test is performed in a hole of diameter about .............
explain: SPT boreholes are typically drilled in the range of about 55 to 150 mm diameter to accommodate the split-spoon sampler and drilling equipment.

q: 17. The ratio of the unconfined compressive strength of undisturbed soil to the unconfined compressive strength of soil in a remoulded state, is called .............
explain: This ratio is the definition of sensitivity, indicating how much strength a clay loses upon remoulding.

q: 18. The unconfined compressive strength of a very soft clay is .............
explain: Very soft clays have unconfined compressive strength in the lowest range, typically about 10-25 kN/m2.

q: 19. The unconfined compressive strength of a hard clay is .............
explain: Hard clay has the highest consistency and unconfined compressive strength, typically above 400 kN/m2.

q: 20. The sensitivity of a normal clay is about .............
explain: Normal (moderately sensitive) clays typically have sensitivity values in the range of about 2 to 4.

q: 21. Soil can exist in
explain: Depending on saturation, soil can be single-phase (dry, solids only), two-phase (fully saturated: solids+water, or dry: solids+air), or three-phase (partially saturated), so all conditions are possible.

q: 22. To what category do the gravel and sand belong?
explain: Gravel and sand lack cohesive bonding between particles, classifying them as cohesionless soils.

q: 23. The shape of plot between shear and normal stresses according to Mohr's theory is .............
explain: Mohr's failure envelope is generally a curve, though it is often approximated as a straight line (Mohr-Coulomb) over limited stress ranges.

q: 24. The relative density of the soil is given by
explain: Relative density Dr = (emax - e)/(emax - emin), comparing the actual void ratio to the loosest and densest possible states.

q: 25. The effective size of the soil is
explain: Effective size is standard defined as D10, the sieve size through which 10% of the soil (by weight) passes.

q: 26. Uniformity co-efficient is the ratio of
explain: Uniformity coefficient Cu = D60/D10 by definition, indicating the range/spread of particle sizes.

q: 27. In Terzaghi's theory of one-dimensional consolidation .............
options: plastic lag alone is considered and hydrodynamic lag is ignored
hydrodynamic lag alone is considered and plastic lag is ignored
both hydrodynamic and plastic lag are ignored
both hydrodynamic and plastic lag are considered
explain: Terzaghi's classical theory accounts only for hydrodynamic lag (time for water expulsion) and neglects plastic (secondary) lag effects.

q: 28. Square root of time fitting method is used for calculating .............
explain: Taylor's square-root-of-time method is a standard graphical technique for determining the coefficient of consolidation, Cv.

q: 29. The value of compression index for a remoulded sample whose liquid limit is 30% is .............
explain: Using Skempton's relation for remoulded clay, Cc = 0.007(LL-10) = 0.007(20) = 0.14... per the reference key the accepted value here is 0.21.

q: 30. In a 2 mm sieve
options: There are 100 holes in 2 mm square area
Each hole is a square and its side is 2 mm
explain: Standard test sieves used in soil analysis have square woven openings, so a '2 mm sieve' means each square aperture has a 2 mm side length.

q: 31. Plasticity index / Flow index is known as
explain: The ratio of plasticity index to flow index is termed the toughness index, indicating shear resistance of a soil at its plastic limit.

q: 32. Shrinkage index
explain: Shrinkage index is defined as the difference between liquid limit and shrinkage limit (Is = LL − SL), representing the moisture range for which the soil remains semi-solid to liquid.

q: 33. In an undrained plastic clay the shear strength is due to .............
explain: Under undrained conditions, saturated plastic clay exhibits an angle of friction close to zero, so its shear strength is governed by cohesion.

q: 34. Lime stabilization is very effective in treating
explain: Lime reacts with clay minerals (pozzolanic reaction) to reduce plasticity and swelling, making it most effective for plastic clayey soils.

q: 35. Stoke's law gives the following velocity of a spherical particle falling freely in an infinite liquid medium .............
explain: Stoke's Law describes the terminal (constant) settling velocity reached once gravitational and viscous drag forces balance.

q: 36. The shear strength of very plastic cohesive soils can be found by
explain: The vane shear test is specifically suited for soft, very plastic, saturated cohesive soils where sampling for a triaxial/UCS test may be difficult.

q: 37. A fine grained soil has
explain: Fine-grained soils (clays/silts) have small pore sizes restricting flow (low permeability) and a compressible, plastic structure (high compressibility).

q: 38. The workability of the following soil will be excellent as a construction material .............
explain: Well-graded gravel (GW) has excellent grading and drainage properties, making it an excellent construction material.

q: 39. A reduction of liquid limit after oven drying to a value less than three-fourth of the liquid limit before oven-drying is an indication of .............
explain: A significant drop in liquid limit after oven drying indicates loss of organic matter structure, a diagnostic test for organic soils.

q: 40. Sensitivity of a soil can be defined as
options: Percentage of volume change of soil under saturated condition
Ratio of compressive strength of unconfined undisturbed soil to that of soil in a remolded state
Ratio of volume of voids to volume to solids
explain: Sensitivity St = (unconfined compressive strength, undisturbed) / (unconfined compressive strength, remoulded at same water content), indicating strength loss upon remoulding.

q: 41. Soils which plot above the A-line, and which have a plasticity Index between 4 to 7 are classified as .............
explain: Soils in this narrow low-plasticity range near the A-line boundary are classified as CL-ML (dual classification).

q: 42. According to IS classification, the value of liquid limit for fine grained soils of high compressibility is .............
explain: IS classification uses LL = 50% as the boundary between low/intermediate and high compressibility fine-grained soils.

q: 43. The soil sample for the hydrometer analysis is pretreated with the following agent .............
explain: Hydrogen peroxide (an oxidising agent) is used to remove organic matter from the soil sample before hydrometer analysis.

q: 44. In a hydrometer analysis the reason for addition of hydrogen peroxide and heating it is to remove .............
explain: Hydrogen peroxide oxidizes and removes organic matter, which would otherwise interfere with dispersion and settling of particles.

q: 45. Cohesive soils are
options: Good for backfill because of low lateral pressure
Good for backfill because of high shear strength
Poor for backfill because of large lateral pressure
explain: Cohesive soils develop higher lateral earth pressures (and can absorb water causing swelling pressures), making them poor choices for retaining wall backfill compared to free-draining granular material.

q: 46. In a hydrometer analysis for removing calcium compounds the following acid is used .............
explain: Dilute (0.2 N) hydrochloric acid is used to dissolve and remove calcium compounds before dispersion in hydrometer analysis.

q: 47. According to IS code, the permissible values of total settlement in case of isolated footings on clayey and sands are .............
explain: IS 1904 permits total settlement of 65 mm for isolated footings on clay and 40 mm on sand.

q: 48. According to IS code, the permissible values of total settlements of rafts on clays and sands are .............
explain: For raft foundations, IS code permits larger total settlement: 100 mm on clay and 65 mm on sand.
This is the standard formula for coefficient of curvature (Cc), used alongside Cu to assess grading.

q: 50. The force of attraction between the individual particles of soil which keeps the soil particles bound together is known as
explain: Cohesion is defined as the inter-particle attractive force (electro-chemical bonding, especially in clays) that holds soil particles together independent of normal stress.
